status: DRAFT: not registered; no recorded run
recording: self-contained runtime gate (code/gate.py, a copy of experiments/2026-11-18-range-pruning/code/gate.py at 0dc7b3b, amendments 1 and 3) and self-recorded manifests; not recorded by the team runtime
question: How do the exact GPU scorers (range v2 and seeded range-bound pruning) compare with BMP, the exact state-of-the-art CPU method, on the same machine, index, queries and answers, at full scale?
hypothesis: None about the size of the gap. Published single-thread BMP reports 10.5 ms mean for this collection at k=10 on other hardware; our GPU scorers measured 0.49-0.72 ms mean on cuda5. This run replaces that cross-paper indication with a paired same-host measurement
contract: GSP-CAP32-U32GUARDED-NUMERIC-TIES-v1 for the GPU scorers and GSP-CAP32-U64-NUMERIC-TIES-v1 for BMP (uint64 sums); identical answers under the uint32 guard. All passages eligible, ties by original numeric passage ID, cap32 query weights

inputs.rule: checked by whole-file SHA-256 before any scoring, in this order
inputs.bmp_index_provenance: Built with the patched BMP ciff2bmp --bsize 32 (raw block bounds) from the pinned raw CIFF (SHA-256 16b111a409c557b966322c3b093e96a83c54a76e7863a0af4db3d0ae57043953, re-downloaded on cuda2 from the pinned Hugging Face revision and accepted on hash equality) on cuda2, a CIMS host with 251 GB RAM: the build peaked at 44.1 GB (22 min), which cuda5 could not spare; an attempt there pushed other users into swap and was stopped. The 13,448,678,853-byte output was streamed to cuda5; its SHA-256 eaf549b8... was computed on the stream and on the cuda5 file and is equal. No compressed-bound index was built (see implementations.bmp-b32)
inputs.pisa_queries_provenance: code/export_queries.py from the pinned GSP vocabulary; its first 25 lines are byte-identical to the 25-query file of the validated 1M BMP experiment (2026-11-11-bmp-resident-timing)

fixed.host: cuda5 (2 x Xeon E5-2650 v2, RTX 4070 UUID GPU-ab7b89ba-5664-fd05-e352-a4bc034e5ff7)

implementations.bmp-b32: pisa-engine/BMP 67ad8c683fbc0c30145d1ee42c1dffbed8b12332 with the reviewed canonical patch (experiments/2026-11-10-bmp-correctness-fixes) and resident-context overlay (experiments/2026-11-11-bmp-resident-timing), timed by code/project_benchmark_single.rs: the validated project_benchmark adapter with its timed query() and monitor() functions byte-identical and only the second (compressed) index and the raw/compressed interleaving removed, so one 13.4 GB index is resident instead of two (about 24 GB, which risked pushing other users into swap on cuda5). Raw block bounds: the faster layout in the team's 1M timing (compressed 12.11% slower), so the stronger BMP baseline. Pinned Cargo.lock, cargo build --release --locked with cuda5's system Rust. Block size 32, alpha = beta = 1 (exact), one Rayon thread pinned to CPU 0, memory bound to node 0, queries in file order
implementations.gpu: the exact cuda_range_v2 and cuda_range_prune binaries of range-pruning run 20261117-cuda5-prune-04 (built and verified by 20261117-cuda5-prune-03), checked by hash; host thread on CPU 0, local allocation; 256 score threads

timing_boundary: BMP: per query, from the resident index and the query text to the ordered TREC top-k string (cursor creation, query preparation, bounds, scheduling, scoring, top-k), the validated adapter's boundary. GPU: from the parsed (term, weight) pairs to the ordered top-k in host memory, including launches, synchronisation and result transfer. BMP's boundary additionally includes query-text parsing and TREC string construction, which favours the GPU slightly; this is stated wherever the comparison is reported

timing.order: every configuration once per pass, three passes with rotation offsets 0, ceil(n/3), ceil(2n/3)
timing.before_each_process: wait (30 s polls, bounded by the deadline) until other users' CPU use over 5 s is at most CPU_LIMIT cores and, for GPU scorers, no foreign GPU process is active with at least 7000 MiB of device memory free, or, for BMP, at least 20 GiB of host memory is available (BMP holds a 13.4 GB index resident; this avoids pushing other users into swap)
timing.sampling: every 0.5 s: machine CPU time from /proc minus the scorer and the sampler (all processes); nvidia-smi compute processes and per-process activity (GPU scorers); the BMP adapter also records CPU-0 jiffies and frequency before and after every round
timing.eligibility: a timing process is ineligible if other users' CPU use averaged more than CPU_LIMIT cores, or (GPU scorers) a foreign GPU process was active in its released phase or its own was not sampled; a non-zero exit while another GPU process was sampled is a contended failure (ineligible); any other failure stops the run
timing.replacement: ineligible processes are kept under raw/ineligible/ and replaced without a count limit; the run stops at a 12-hour wall-clock deadline and can be resumed from the same commit
timing.cpu_limit_rationale: the value of the range-pruning experiment; BMP is single-threaded and pinned to CPU 0, and the adapter's CPU-0 records allow reporting how much of CPU 0 was used by others

correctness_gate: BMP's unit tests; two deliberate runtime-gate rejections (BMP CPU, v2 score threads); BMP once on all 500 queries equal to the CPU reference; every timing process's answers equal to the CPU reference. The GPU binaries' fixtures and correctness are those of range-pruning runs 03/04 (logs/reuse.txt). Any mismatch stops the run

analysis.primary: bmp-b32 / GPU scorer for v2-w1024, prune-w1024-s64 and prune-w256-s64: geometric mean over (process, query) pairs of median_bmp / median_gpu, paired by process index and query
analysis.secondary: descriptive median, mean, p95, p99 per configuration; BMP's CPU-0 busy share per process from its own /proc/stat snapshots
analysis.interval: crossed process/query bootstrap, 10,000 draws, seed 20261118, percentile 2.5/97.5; conditional on this session and the calibration queries

limits: one host; BMP single-threaded (its published setting), on a 2013 server CPU; GPU a 2023 consumer card
BMP's timing boundary includes query-text parsing and TREC output, the GPU's does not
shared machine; calibration queries only; held-out untouched
BMP is the exact state of the art; approximate methods (e.g. Seismic) are not compared
